paper_sections.title: Ventromedial Prefrontal Cortex Encodes Emotional Value
Effects of emotion experience and regulation
Neural response to normative valence by condition
pvmPFC activation is associated with differences in behavioral ratings

description.value: The study investigated how cognitive reappraisal of positive and negative emotional images affects valuation-related activity in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex, and whether vmPFC activity tracks subjective and normative emotional value.

design.value: Two independent experimental samples of human participants performed a cognitive reappraisal task while undergoing fMRI. Participants were instructed either to experience their emotions naturally or to regulate them using cognitive reappraisal.

description.value: Participants in Exp2 scored at 27 or higher on the Folstein Mini-Mental State Examination.

task_description.value: Participants viewed images from the International Affective Picture System and were asked either to regulate their emotions using cognitive reappraisal or to experience their emotions naturally.

instructions.value: For the Experience condition, participants were instructed to experience their emotions naturally. For the Regulate condition, participants were asked to emotionally detach themselves from the image.

stimuli.value: Images from the International Affective Picture System, categorized as positive, negative, or neutral based on normative IAPS ratings.

description.value: Functional data were acquired using a gradient-echo inverse-spiral pulse sequence; 30 axial slices parallel to the AC–PC plane; FOV = 256 mm; flip angle = 60°; voxel size = 4 × 4 × 4 mm. Each run contained 288 volumes; the first six volumes were discarded.
Functional data were acquired with TE = 31 ms; flip angle = 90°; 34 slices; voxel size = 3.75 × 3.75 × 3.8 mm. Each run contained 238 volumes; the first six volumes were discarded.
A high-resolution inversion-recovery prepared SPGR anatomical image was used for normalization and coregistration of the functional data; whole brain coverage with 1 × 1 × 1 mm voxels.
A high-resolution inversion-recovery prepared SPGR anatomical image was used for normalization and coregistration of the functional data.
fMRI preprocessing included motion correction, brain extraction, spatial smoothing, high-pass filtering, and normalization to standard space.

steps.value: spatial smoothing using an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 6 mm (FWHM)
functional images were normalized using transforms estimated from each participant's own high-resolution anatomical image and FSL's MNI template using FLIRT

model_settings.value: First-level models corrected for local autocorrelation; second-level fixed-effects model combined data across runs within a participant; third-level mixed-effects analysis (FLAME 1) modeled effects across participants. Regressors modeled the 8 s implementation period, with nuisance regressors for initial picture presentation and response period.

level.value: first-level, second level, and third level

estimator.value: restricted maximum likelihood estimation for the behavioral repeated measures multilevel model

model_settings.value: The model included experiment number, IAPS normative ratings, condition, the interaction of IAPS normative ratings and condition, and trial-by-trial estimates of pvmPFC activation as independent variables and trial-by-trial valence ratings as the dependent variable.
